newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major Japan public fund bought US T-notes--bankers.
newsitem.headline: Major Japan public fund bought US T-notes--bankers.

text.p: A major Japanese public fund body, possibly the Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo), appeared to have bought medium-term U.S. Treasury notes this week, bankers in Tokyo said on Thursday.

"Kampo seemed to have bought medium-term U.S. T-notes this week during Tokyo trading hours when the dollar was around 115.10-20 yen," a senior banker said. The dollar/yen rate traded around that range on Tuesday and Wednesday in Tokyo.
A Kampo official declined to comment on the fund body's investments, saying it would invite speculation and affect the market.

Kampo, which is regarded as one of the world's biggest investors, held a total 95.88 trillion yen worth of funds as of the end of November. Of the total, it held 3.55 trillion yen worth of foreign bonds, the official said.

Kampo has been able to use currency forward transactions to hedge its holdings of foreign currency-denominated bonds from May 1995 following the revision of a law, but the official said that it has not done so yet.
Traders said Treasury prices were well-bid in Tokyo on Thursday, with the key 30-year bond standing at 95-27/32, yielding 6.83 percent, in late trade compared with 95-21/32 at the close in New York.

Traders said some Japanese life insurance firms may have taken profits from Treasuries this week for the purpose of covering their losses from ailing Japanese share prices ahead of book closings this fiscal year. But the amount of the sales was still believed to be relatively small.
Meanwhile, other Japanese participants, including trust banks and public funds, showed strong buying interest and were detected buying on falls, traders said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
